exposure: metabolic acidosis at birth (pH <7.05 or <7.10 and base deficit >=12)
outcome: reduced Apgar scores (7, 8, and 9) at 1, 5, and 10 minutes
cohort: The study included 81,861 term, non-malformed infants born in Sweden between 2008 and 2013, with available information from cord blood gas analyses and Apgar scores of 7-10.
finding: Metabolic acidosis at birth is significantly associated with increased risks of reduced Apgar scores (7-9) at 5 and 10 minutes, even within the normal range, and also influences neonatal morbidity.
